code.originalText: Establishing care for left chest wall pain and breathlessness on exertion since an old penetrating chest wound, with heavy episodic drinking and recent bereavement found at the visit: chest X-ray, spirometry, liver tests, PEth, AUDIT, PHQ-9, safety assessment, and a pulmonology consultation

text.paragraph: The patient attends this visit for establishing care for left chest wall pain and breathlessness on exertion since an old penetrating chest wound, with heavy episodic drinking and recent bereavement found at the visit: chest X-ray, spirometry, liver tests, PEth, AUDIT, PHQ-9, safety assessment, and a pulmonology consultation. [S]

[S]

list.item: Left chest wall pain at the scar of an old penetrating arrow wound, with breathlessness on exertion and a reduced FVC (78 percent predicted) with a normal FEV1/FVC ratio, and heavy episodic drinking (AUDIT 19, PEth 236 ng/mL), found at intake; cause and extent under evaluation with a pulmonology consultation and an addiction medicine assessment: active, confirmed [S]

Bereavement five months after the death of his closest companion since boyhood, with depressive symptoms (PHQ-9 12, item 9 scored 0) that do not meet criteria for a major depressive episode; prolonged grief disorder cannot be diagnosed before twelve months: active, confirmed [S]

Chest: chest X-ray and spirometry at intake; CT of the chest and lung volumes with diffusing capacity and a six-minute walk at the consultation; repeat spirometry after two to three months of the exercise program. Guideline: Standardization of Spirometry 2019 Update. An Official American Thoracic Society and European Respiratory Society Technical Statement (2019); ERS/ATS technical standard on interpretive strategies for routine lung function tests (2022); British Thoracic Society Guideline for pleural disease (2023) [S]

Pulmonology consultation for chest wall pain and reduced lung function after a penetrating chest wound: a retained fragment, pleural thickening or trapped lung, the need for surgery, pain treatment without opioids, fitness for heavy exertion, and lung function follow-up. Guideline: ERS/ATS technical standard on interpretive strategies for routine lung function tests (2022); British Thoracic Society Guideline for pleural disease (2023) [S]

Chest wall pain: acetaminophen up to 2,000 mg a day; no opioids, tramadol, gabapentinoids or benzodiazepines while he drinks heavily; no regular anti-inflammatory tablets with heavy drinking. Guideline: CDC Clinical Practice Guideline for Prescribing Opioids for Pain - United States, 2022 (2022) [S]

Alcohol: AUDIT, DSM-5-TR criteria and PEth with consent; liver tests; brief counseling at intake and sessions with the clinic's addiction medicine clinician; withdrawal risk assessed (no withdrawal expected with his pattern); thiamine for three months; PEth and liver tests at follow-up. Guideline: Unhealthy Alcohol Use in Adolescents and Adults: Screening and Behavioral Counseling Interventions (2018); The American Psychiatric Association Practice Guideline for the Pharmacological Treatment of Patients With Alcohol Use Disorder (2018); VA/DoD Clinical Practice Guideline for the Management of Substance Use Disorders (2021) [S]

Grief and mood: sessions with the clinic's behavioral health clinician, sleep routine, PHQ-9 every four to six weeks; reassess for prolonged grief disorder only if intense grief persists beyond twelve months; antidepressant only if a major depressive episode develops. Guideline: Prolonged Grief Disorder (DSM-5-TR criteria for patients and families) (2022); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, depression monograph (2026); Depression and Suicide Risk in Adults: Screening (2023) [S]

Safety: a structured safety assessment, the service pistol kept in the armory off duty and never carried after drinking, a written safety plan, the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline, and safety review at every visit. Guideline: VA/DoD Clinical Practice Guideline for Assessment and Management of Patients at Risk for Suicide (2024); Depression and Suicide Risk in Adults: Screening (2023) [S]
